blocks.text: Introduction

Assalam o alaikum bachon! Aaj hum Unit 14 shuru kar rahe hain: Vectors in Space, yani teen dimensions (lambai, chaurai aur unchai) mein vectors. Ab tak aap ne vectors kaghaz ki satah par, yani do dimensions mein, parhe hain. Lekin hamari asal duniya teen dimensional hai: kamre mein urti hui makkhi sirf aage-peeche aur daayen-baayen nahin, upar-neeche bhi jaati hai. Is liye physics aur engineering mein teen coordinates wale vectors har jagah kaam aate hain. Is sabaq mein hum pehle purani baatein dohraayenge, phir unhein space mein le jaayenge.

Kitab ka introduction batata hai ke is unit mein hum teen dimensional space mein rectangular coordinate system (aapas mein perpendicular teen axes wala nizaam) dekhenge, aur space mein vectors par bunyadi operations seekhenge. Phir do vectors ka dot product (scalar product) aur cross product (vector product) aur un ka geometric matlab samjhenge. Kitab in ke amali istemaal par zor deti hai, maslan in se triangle aur parallelogram ka area kaise nikalta hai. Aakhir mein hum dekhenge ke physics mein vectors kitne zaroori hain: forces, velocities aur doosri physical quantities ka hisaab inhi se hota hai, jaise kisi constant force ka kisi object ko ek diye gaye vector ke saath hilaane mein kiya gaya work.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is unit ka naqsha: 14.1 mein purane vectors yaad karke unhein space mein le jaate hain (do ki jagah teen coordinates); 14.2 dot product; 14.3 cross product; 14.4 scalar triple product.
Notation (likhne ka tareeqa): kitab vector ke harf ke neeche line lagati hai, jaise \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{i}\). Kuch kitaabein bold harf ya teer \(\vec{u}\) istemaal karti hain; matlab sab ka ek hi hai. \(\underline{AB}\) woh vector hai jo \(A\) se shuru ho kar \(B\) par khatam hota hai. Apni copy mein vector par hamesha nishaan (line ya teer) lagaiye; baghair nishaan ke harf sirf ek number samjha jaata hai, aur examiner yahan number kaat leta hai.

Pichhli classes mein humne do bunyadi quantities parhi thi: scalars aur vectors. Scalar woh quantity hai jis ki sirf magnitude (miqdaar ya size) hoti hai, jaise mass, time, density, temperature, length, volume, speed, work waghaira. Doosri taraf vector woh quantity hai jis ki magnitude bhi hoti hai aur direction (simt) bhi, jaise displacement, velocity, acceleration, weight, force, momentum, electric aur magnetic fields waghaira.

Geometry ki zabaan mein vector ko ek directed line segment (simt wala seedha tukra) \(\underline{AB}\) se dikhaya jaata hai, jis ka initial point (shuru ka nuqta) \(A\) aur terminal point (aakhri nuqta) \(B\) hota hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Teer hi kyun? Teer ki lambai magnitude batati hai aur teer ka sira direction. Is liye \(\underline{AB}\) aur \(\underline{BA}\) ki lambai barabar hai lekin simt ulti: \(\underline{BA} = -\underline{AB}\).
Scalar ya vector pehchaanne ka aasaan test: poochiye \"kis simt mein?\". \"5 kg kis simt mein?\" ka koi matlab nahin, is liye mass scalar hai. \"20 N kis simt mein?\" bohat ahem hai (upar dhakka aur neeche dhakka alag cheezein hain), is liye force vector hai.

Do dimensions (\(R^{2}\)) mein vector ke components ek ordered pair (tarteeb wala jora) \([x, y]\) se likhe jaate hain, jis mein dono real numbers hain. Vector \(\underline{u} = [x, y]\) mein \(x\) aur \(y\) ko \(\underline{u}\) ke components (hisse) kehte hain. Ordered ka matlab hai ke tarteeb ahem hai: \([2, 5]\) aur \([5, 2]\) do alag vectors hain.
Addition of vectors: kisi bhi do vectors \(\underline{u} = [x_{1}, y_{1}]\) aur \(\underline{v} = [x_{2}, y_{2}]\) ke liye

blocks.text_alt: u plus v equals x1 plus x2, y1 plus y2

blocks.text: Scalar Multiplication of a vector: \(\underline{u} = [x, y]\) aur kisi real number \(a \in R\) ke liye

blocks.text_alt: a times u equals a x, a y

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dono rules component ba component chalte hain: pehle components aapas mein, doosre components aapas mein. Kabhi bhi pehle component ko doosre ke saath mat jodiye.
\([2, 3] + [4, -1] = [2 + 4,\ 3 + (-1)] = [6, 2]\)
\(3[2, -1] = [3 \times 2,\ 3 \times (-1)] = [6, -3]\)
Tasavvur kijiye: jama karna aisa hai jaise pehle \(\underline{u}\) ke saath chalein phir \(\underline{v}\) ke saath; 3 se zarb dena teer ko teen guna lamba kar deta hai, aur negative number teer ko ulta bhi kar deta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Neeche di gayi quantities mein se kaun scalar hai aur kaun vector? Pehle khud sochiye, phir jawab dekhiye: (1) ek kamre ka temperature 30 degree, (2) gaari ki raftaar 60 km/h, (3) gaari ka 60 km/h shumaal ki taraf chalna, (4) kitaab ka weight.
Jawab: (1) scalar, (2) scalar (speed mein simt nahin), (3) vector (velocity, simt di hui hai), (4) vector, kyunke weight hamesha neeche ki taraf zameen ki simt mein lagta hai. Yaad rakhiye: speed scalar hai, velocity vector.

Kyun: component ba component jama karna kyun theek hai? Socho aap pehle 2 qadam mashriq (east) aur 3 qadam shumaal (north) chale, phir 4 qadam mashriq aur 1 qadam junoob (south) chale. Kul mashriq ki taraf 2 + 4 = 6 qadam aur shumaal ki taraf 3 - 1 = 2 qadam. Mashriq wale qadam sirf mashriq walon se judte hain aur shumaal wale sirf shumaal walon se. Yahi baat vector addition ka rule kehta hai: \([2, 3] + [4, -1] = [6, 2]\).

Equal Vectors: \(R^{2}\) ke do vectors \(\underline{u} = [x_{1}, y_{1}]\) aur \(\underline{v} = [x_{2}, y_{2}]\) tab aur sirf tab barabar kehlate hain jab un ke components barabar hon. Yani \([x_{1}, y_{1}] = [x_{2}, y_{2}]\) tab aur sirf tab jab \(x_{1} = x_{2}\) aur \(y_{1} = y_{2}\); phir hum likhte hain \(\underline{u} = \underline{v}\).
Doosre alfaaz mein, do vectors barabar hain agar un ki magnitude bhi same ho aur direction bhi same ho.

blocks.alt: Two arrows of the same length pointing in the same direction (up and to the left): AB from A to B and CD from C to D, drawn side by side.
blocks.caption: Equal vectors AB and CD: same length and same direction, different positions (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Figure mein \(\underline{AB}\) aur \(\underline{CD}\) alag alag jagah se shuru hote hain, phir bhi barabar hain, kyunke vector ke liye sirf lambai aur simt maayne rakhti hai, jagah nahin. Aap vector ko kahin bhi khiska sakte hain, bas usay ghumaana ya khenchna nahin. Jaise do bachay alag alag gharon se nikal kar dono 2 km shumaal (north) ki taraf chalein: dono ka displacement barabar hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Hamari practice.) Agar \([a + 1,\ 4] = [3,\ b - 2]\) ho to \(a\) aur \(b\) nikaaliye.
Barabar vectors ke components barabar hote hain, is liye pehla component pehle ke barabar aur doosra doosre ke barabar rakhenge:
\(a + 1 = 3 \Rightarrow a = 2\)
\(4 = b - 2 \Rightarrow b = 6\)
Tasdeeq: \([2 + 1,\ 4] = [3, 4]\) aur \([3,\ 6 - 2] = [3, 4]\). Dono barabar. Ek vector equation asal mein do (space mein teen) aam equations ka majmooa hai.

Parallel Vectors: do vectors tab aur sirf tab parallel hain jab ek doosre ka non-zero scalar multiple ho (yani ek ko kisi ghair sifar number se zarb dein to doosra mil jaaye).
Misaal ke taur par vectors \(-\underline{AB}\) aur \(\frac{3}{2}\underline{AB}\) dono \(\underline{AB}\) ke parallel hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yeh jumla \"parallel to \(\underline{AB} - \underline{BA}\)\" par khatam karti hai. Figure mein \(\underline{AB}\), \(-\underline{AB}\) aur \(\frac{3}{2}\underline{AB}\) bane hain, is liye asal matlab yeh hai ke \(-\underline{AB}\) aur \(\frac{3}{2}\underline{AB}\) dono \(\underline{AB}\) ke parallel hain. (Waise \(\underline{BA} = -\underline{AB}\) hai, is liye chhapa hua \(\underline{AB} - \underline{BA} = 2\underline{AB}\) banta hai jo bhi parallel hai, lekin jumle ka maqsad yeh nahin.)

blocks.alt: Three arrows on parallel slanting lines: AB pointing up to the right, minus AB of the same length pointing down to the left, and three halves AB pointing up to the right and one and a half times as long.
blocks.caption: Parallel vectors AB, −AB and (3/2)AB (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Parallel hone ka test kaise karein? Component ko component se divide kijiye. Agar saare ratios barabar aayen to vectors parallel hain.
\([-3, 6]\) aur \([2, -4]\): \(\frac{-3}{2} = \frac{6}{-4} = -\frac{3}{2}\), is liye \([-3, 6] = -\frac{3}{2}[2, -4]\): parallel.
Positive multiple ho to dono ek hi taraf, negative ho to ulti taraf (jaise figure mein \(-\underline{AB}\)).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Kya \([4, 6]\) aur \([6, 9]\) parallel hain? Aur \([4, 6]\) aur \([6, 8]\)?
Jawab: pehle jore mein \(\frac{6}{4} = \frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2}\), is liye parallel. Doosre mein \(\frac{6}{4} = 1.5\) lekin \(\frac{8}{6} \approx 1.33\), ratios barabar nahin, is liye parallel nahin.
Magnitude of a Vector

2D mein kisi vector ki magnitude (norm ya length) us vector ki origin se us point tak ki lambai hai jise vector dikhata hai. \(R^{2}\) ke kisi bhi vector \(\underline{u} = [x, y]\) ke liye hum magnitude ko point \(P(x, y)\) ka origin \(O\) se faasla (distance) define karte hain.

blocks.text_alt: magnitude of OP equals magnitude of u equals the square root of x squared plus y squared

blocks.alt: x- and y-axes. A cyan line from the origin to the point P(x, y), with an arrowhead at its middle, is labelled square root of x squared plus y squared. A vertical cyan line of length y drops from P to the x-axis; the distance along the x-axis is x.
blocks.caption: Magnitude of u = [x, y]: the length OP of the hypotenuse, √(x² + y²) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh \(\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) aaya kahan se? Figure dekhiye: right triangle ke do chhote sides (legs) \(x\) aur \(y\) hain aur \(OP\) hypotenuse (sab se lamba side, right angle ke saamne) hai. Pythagoras theorem kehta hai \(OP^{2} = x^{2} + y^{2}\), is liye \(OP = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\). Bas, magnitude ka formula asal mein Pythagoras hi hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin.)
\(|[3, 4]| = \sqrt{3^{2} + 4^{2}} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5\)
\(|[-5, 12]| = \sqrt{(-5)^{2} + 12^{2}} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13\)
Dekhiye: \(-5\) ka square bhi \(+25\) hai. Lambai kabhi negative nahin hoti, is liye component ka sign magnitude par asar nahin karta.

Ab hum teen dimensional space mein vectors ke kuch mathematical operations seekhenge. Yahi sab baatein aage teen coordinates ke saath dobara aayengi, bas har jagah ek component ziyada hoga. Is liye agar aaj ka 2D wala hissa achhi tarah samajh aa gaya to 3D bilkul aasaan lagega: jama, scalar se zarb, barabari, parallel hona aur magnitude, sab ke rules wahi rahenge. Magnitude mein bhi Pythagoras do dafa lagega aur formula \(\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}\) ban jaayega, jo hum 14.1.4 mein dekhenge.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: \(|\underline{u} + \underline{v}|\) aam taur par \(|\underline{u}| + |\underline{v}|\) ke barabar nahin hota. \([3, 0] + [0, 4] = [3, 4]\) ki magnitude 5 hai, 7 nahin. Pehle vectors jama kijiye, phir magnitude nikaaliye.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
Scalar ki sirf magnitude hoti hai; vector ki magnitude aur direction dono.
\(\underline{AB}\) \(A\) se shuru, \(B\) par khatam; \(\underline{BA} = -\underline{AB}\).
Jama aur scalar se zarb component ba component.
Equal vectors: components barabar, yani lambai aur simt dono same.
Parallel vectors: ek doosre ka non-zero scalar multiple.
\(|[x, y]| = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) (Pythagoras).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
Vectors ki jagah magnitudes jama kar dena: \(|[3, 0] + [0, 4]|\) ko \(3 + 4 = 7\) likhna. Sahi jawab 5 hai.
Negative component ka square negative likh dena: \((-5)^{2} = 25\) hai, \(-25\) nahin.
\(\underline{AB}\) aur \(\underline{BA}\) ko barabar samajhna: dono ki simt ulti hai.
Vector ke harf par nishaan (line ya teer) na lagana.
